work.title: Persuading Receivers One at a Time

claims.label: Proposition 3
claims.gist: Public signals are optimal for sequential receivers with aligned payoffs.
claims.statement: When receivers act in sequence and their payoffs are aligned, a public signal achieves the sender's optimal value among all private signal structures.
conditions: receivers act in a fixed order

result.summary: The optimality argument checked step by step; no defect found.
result.search_scope: The construction in Appendix A, checked on games with two receivers, three states and binary actions.
result.limits: Does not cover misaligned receivers. Supplement steps checked in the working-paper version only.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.

reproduction.detail: The evidence package reruns with one command (Python 3.12, standard library only).

claims.label: Proposition 6
claims.gist: The optimal public signal needs at most as many messages as actions.
claims.statement: Some optimal public signal uses no more messages than the number of action profiles.

result.summary: No instance required more messages among those checked.
result.search_scope: Two receivers, up to four states and binary actions; optimal signals computed by linear programming.
result.limits: The general argument relies on Supplement S1, checked in the working-paper version only.

vor_check.detail: Statement and definitions checked on rendered pages; the proof compared in extracted text only.
